cohort: 10,040,416 births, including 16,126 with umbilical cord prolapse
finding: Umbilical cord prolapse is associated with an increased risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including placental abruption, excessive bleeding, Cesarean sections, lower Apgar scores, requiring assisted ventilation, neonatal seizures, hyaline membrane disease, and fetal injuries.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a greater risk of fetal injuries than vaginal delivery in women with UCP.
